# Task bank report, group 3: arithmetic (2026-10-12)

Scope: four sources plus two comparisons (MIB arithmetic, LLM_Modularity add_sub). Everything is tier 1, model-independent, capped at 2,000 items per task, seed 42. Scripts: `scripts/task_bank/{fetch,convert}_<source_id>.py` (+ `_arith_common.py`); test: `PYTHONPATH=. python tests/verify_task_bank_arithmetic.py` (passes; also checked that rerunning all converters reproduces identical task files). Token-length diagnostic: prefix + problem + concatenation (no chat template) under the Qwen3.5 tokenizer (`Qwen/Qwen3.5-2B` tokenizer.json, same for 4B). "Single-token answers" = the answer adds exactly one token when appended to the clean prompt (so the leading space counts as a token where Qwen splits it). All configs use `force_base_evaluation: true` (raw text, no chat template), since the arithmetic prompts of these sources are raw completions; LLM_Modularity's own arithmetic tasks instead use the chat template with an instruction.

## 1. devarda_arithmetic (de Varda et al.; converted, 6 tasks)

What: MIT repo https://github.com/Andrea-de-Varda/arithmetic-dataset, pinned commit `19d5bcf5b31aa1d8c37ff3161eaba782d1a7a8fb`, downloaded 2026-10-12. Paper: arXiv 2609.04463 (BibTeX from the arXiv export; the repo is cited separately as the data release, entry assembled from repo metadata because no canonical export exists). Licence: README.md says "MIT License"; there is no LICENSE file (recorded as the source). `redistribute: yes`.

Generation: `python -I generate_arithmetic_data.py -n 10000 --seed 42` (defaults: 50/50 terms, 50/50 digits, carry 0.5) reproduces the committed `data/json/*.json` exactly for all six formats (checked, num2words 0.5.14). The generated output is frozen in raw/devarda_arithmetic/generated (sha256 in the registry). The repo ships six formats, not five: numeric, english, spanish, italian, embedded (digits) and embedded_verbal (number words in the story); all six are converted.

Counterfactuals: only `generate_arithmetic_counterfactual.py` exists, and it covers the numeric format only. The committed `arith_dataset_numeric_counterfactual.json` is a different 5,000-problem sample (first item 37 - 63 + 73), not the 10,000 seed-42 set, so it is not used. Counterfactuals for all six formats exist in the sense that the repo's own `DatasetFormatter` can format a flipped problem in every format; the converter parses operands and operators from the numeric prompt, flips every operator, recomputes the result, and formats x' and y' with the repo formatter. For the verbal formats this swaps the words plus/minus, más/menos, più/meno. Clean prompts and answers regenerated this way equal the committed files for every item and format (asserted).

Embedded formats: the formatter picks names, object and template from a sha256 seed over id|operands|operators, so a flipped problem would get a different cast; the converter replays the clean problem's seed so characters and object are shared. The story template still changes (addition and subtraction use different template lists), so the embedded corruption is not a minimal edit. Length match: 52.6% (embedded) and 52.1% (embedded_verbal) with the replay, versus 17.2% and 17.4% for the repo-verbatim corruption (reported in the registry as `len_match_share_qwen35_repo_verbatim_corruption`). Expect most embedded items to be removed by the run-time length filter; 2,000 is a cap, so the pool can be widened (the eligible pool is 7,037 ids). The embedded subtraction templates 'difference' (about 2/5 of subtraction stories) ask for the subtrahend or minuend rather than the result; y is taken from the formatter, so the answer is the one the story asks for.

Negative results: 2,925 of the 10,000 problems have a negative result after the flip (a+b flipped to a-b with a<b, or 3-term cases); these are dropped for all formats, because the embedded stories cannot express them and verbal answers like "minus ninety-seven" collide with the operator word "minus". A further 38 problems where y equals y' in some format (e.g. x - a + a flipped to x + a - a) are dropped. Eligible pool 7,037; as a consequence the pool over-represents items whose clean problem is a subtraction (additions flip negative often) and 3-term "++" is rare (36 of 2,000). Zero is kept (not negative).

Sampling: 2,000 ids, proportional allocation over strata (n_terms, n_digits, has_carry, operator pattern), largest-remainder rounding, within-stratum shuffle with seed 42; the same ids in all six formats (sidecars `tasks/devarda_arithmetic/<task>.ids.txt`, also `ids.txt`). has_carry refers to the clean problem only. Realised mix: each of the 8 (terms, digits, carry) cells holds 200-317 items; operator patterns: - 545, -+ 482, +- 438, + 412, -- 87, ++ 36.

Prompt framing: `eval_models.py` appends nothing for numeric/english/spanish/italian and `" The answer is"` for both embedded formats (PROMPT_SUFFIXES); an optional `--one-shot` flag prepends a per-format exemplar (ONE_SHOT_EXAMPLES, e.g. "7 + 5 = 12\n"). The repo's standard evaluation is zero-shot by default; the paper's attribution uses one exemplar in the target format (read via a summariser of the arXiv HTML, so verify in the paper). The configs therefore set `prefix` to the exemplar and `concatenation` to the suffix; set `prefix: null` for zero-shot. Answers keep the leading space (" 73"); numeric and embedded answer in digits, english/spanish/italian/embedded_verbal in words. Digit answers need 1 token for the space-less case only; in Qwen the space is a separate token.

Tasks (family; raw n; converted; length match; single-token answers): numeric (arithmetic_addsub_numeric; 10,000; 2,000; 100%; 0%), english (arithmetic_addsub_verbal_en; 100%; 14.1%), spanish (..._es; 100%; 9.0%), italian (..._it; 100%; 7.9%), embedded (arithmetic_addsub_wordproblem; 52.6%; 0%), embedded_verbal (arithmetic_addsub_wordproblem_verbal; 52.1%; 13.4%).

Uncertainties: whether the paper's counterfactuals for the verbal and embedded formats equal ours (the repo does not contain them; the paper page does not describe them); the one-shot framing; the negative-result exclusion changes the item distribution relative to the paper (it filtered by tokenised length and identical outputs, and kept incorrect items); the ids here are repo ids (prob_000000...) of the original 10,000.

## 2. nikankin_arithmetic (Nikankin et al., ICLR 2025; converted, 4 tasks)

Repo https://github.com/technion-cs-nlp/llm-arithmetic-heuristics, commit `accf6b2bca7e1145520e96d0ceb60beb6b769c05`, MIT (LICENSE, Copyright 2024 technion-cs-nlp), redistribute yes. Paper arXiv 2410.21272; the BibTeX is the arXiv export (OpenReview and DBLP were blocked by a bot challenge from this machine); venue ICLR 2025 comes from the repo README.

Data: no prompt files are released. Prompts are generated at run time (`prompt_generation.py`): "x{op}y=" without spaces, four operators (+ - * /), operands 0..299 (notebook: max_op=300, set_deterministic(42)), second-operand ranges from `_get_operand_range`, results 0..999 (Llama-3 single-token range), then filtered by Llama-3's own correctness (model-dependent). Their patching pairs each prompt with a random other prompt; the notebook comment says corrupt prompts differ in operator and/or operands. Our tier-1 variant re-implements the model-independent part (seed 42): clean prompt sampled stratified by operand digit counts; partner = random prompt of the same operator with the same digit counts of both operands and a different answer (so y != y' holds by construction, and lengths match). Division keeps exact integer quotients only (the original also keeps non-integer quotients and truncates in the check). The Llama-3 correctness filter is not applied.

Tasks (all family arithmetic_<op>_numeric_operand_swap; length match 100% in all): add (pool 90,000; 2,000; single-token answers 0.1%), sub (45,150; 2,000; 6.3%), mul (5,784; 2,000; 11.9%), div (2,048; 1,717; 48.3%). Division has 1,717 rather than 2,000 because the pool has only 2,048 exact quotients and 283 clean prompts have no partner (for instance 3-digit x with 3-digit y only admits x=y, answer 1). No prefix, concatenation or chat template (the original is a bare "x+y=" completion); answers have no leading space ("=570"). Because the Qwen tokenizer splits digits, "single-token" answers are only 1-digit results.

Neuron index files: not released. `.gitignore` excludes `*.pt`, `per_neuron_*`, `mlp_input_*`, `data/mean_cache*`, and the repo has no `data/` directory; the per-neuron results are produced by `script_per_neuron_analysis.py` / `script_topk_neuron_eval.py` on Llama-3-8B/70B (and Pythia-6.9B) with GPUs. So there is nothing to convert for the neuron-list pass from this repo, and the lists would be for Llama tokenisers anyway (note that the format-invariant repo, section 4, commits importance .pt and heuristics JSON files for Llama-3).

## 3. stolfo_arithmetic (Stolfo, Belinkov & Sachan, EMNLP 2023; converted, 5 tasks)

Repo https://github.com/alestolfo/lm-arithmetic, commit `ec00a0445738857db228d85a64eaf94e2bdf53b3`, MIT (LICENSE, Copyright 2023 Alessandro Stolfo), redistribute yes. BibTeX: ACL Anthology `2023.emnlp-main.435` (EMNLP 2023, pages 7035-7052), checked against the arXiv title and authors.

Data: none released; `interventions/intervention.py` samples prompts at run time (Hydra, GPT-J tokenizer). Six templates per operator (verbatim: "Q: How much is {x} plus {y}? A:", "Q: What is {x} plus {y}? A:", "Q: What is the result of ...", "Q: What is the sum of {x} and {y}? A:", "The sum of {x} and {y} is", "{x} + {y} ="; analogous for minus, times, over). Intervention type 1 = operands change (operand swap), type 2 = operands change but the result is unchanged, type 3 = operator change. Our seed-42 re-implementation (the repo code needs Hydra, torch and a tokenizer; not run): defaults of conf/config.yaml, max_n=300 (operands 1..300, integer results 1..299), zero-shot, Arabic numerals, templates cycled round-robin, 2,000 items per task. Tasks: add, sub, mul, div (type 1; I additionally require equal digit counts per operand position, as the repo does in its Llama setting, and a different result, which the repo enforces only in that setting), and operator_change (type 3: same operands, a random different operator among + - * /, same template index, both results integers in 1..299 and different). Length match is 100% for every task (the operator words and the digit counts are matched). Single-token answers 0%: answers have a leading space (" 12"), which Qwen tokenises separately. Families: arithmetic_<op>_numeric_operand_swap (same label as the Nikankin tasks, since both are operand-swap tasks of one operator, in numeric format; they differ in template and operand range) and arithmetic_operator_change_numeric.

Not converted: type 2 (no flip), the 'words' representation (the repo's convert_to_words; would add multiword answers, and the formats question is covered by de Varda), three-operand equations (three_operand_questions.json), number-retrieval and LAMA tasks. Say so if you want any of them.

## 4. format_invariant_arithmetic (arXiv 2607.16693; NOT converted, status unverified)

Authors (arXiv): Sharath Naganna, Tanvir Ahmed Sijan, Uddipta Kalita, "Are Arithmetic Heuristic Neurons Form-Invariant? A Mechanistic Analysis of Symbols, Text, and Code in LLMs", 2026, "Under Review"; the repo https://github.com/SharathHN/format-invariant-arithmetic (commit `55ff6e86874c873e1537daf986252d17e764fa36`; commits by SharathHN and sijantanvir) matches the authors. The arXiv page lists CC BY 4.0 for the paper; the repo has no LICENSE file and no licence statement, so licence is unclear and redistribute is treated as no. Hence no items are written. BibTeX: arXiv export.

Fit: rewrites the Nikankin prompts in three forms: plain "x+y=", a Python script ending "Output: Ans = " (floor division "//"), and a word problem ("Tom has X apples and Alice gives him Y apples. So he now has "; analogous for - * /); operands up to 999, trivial cases (operand <= 5 or answer <= 2) excluded; 200 prompts per operator and format, Llama-3 correct only (8B, 3.2-3B, 3.2-1B), stored as .pkl (not unpickled, untrusted) plus a JSON for llama1b datasets_wrong. No corruption pairs in the data (random partners, as in Nikankin). A flipping variant from the templates is easy (as for Nikankin), and the code and word formats add formats the others lack, so this is worth pursuing if the authors confirm a licence. The repo also commits Llama-3 importance .pt files and heuristics JSON per format and operator: candidate material for the neuron-list pass (Llama tokenizer, not Qwen).

## 5. Comparisons only (not converted)

MIB (another agent converts): HF `mib-bench/arithmetic_addition` (revision d56d68b7b1d8f9c7e9a262ec1f89331ed52c7516) and `arithmetic_subtraction` (9eeb7f0f69c2adc131d81200f501a7f83c06fa8b); the dataset cards carry no licence text. Items use the Stolfo template "Q: How much is 27 plus 64? A: " (prompt ends with a space), 2-digit operands, label without space, and a dozen counterfactual types (random, change of ones/tens digit of either operand, carry variants), so the answer flips in most types. This is the closest relative of the Stolfo tasks above (same template family); MIB covers operand swaps of the template-0 form only.

LLM_Modularity (`external/llm_modularity/data/MD/add_sub_2op_symbolic.json` and `_verbal.json`, 1,000 items each): "862 - 158 =" with a corrupted problem that changes one digit of one operand (862 - 128 =), 3-digit operands, answers without leading space, framed as "What is the answer of {problem}? Please directly give the final answer written in digits." through the chat template (no force_base_evaluation); the verbal version uses number words and "written in words, not digits". Corruption: single-digit operand edit, answer flips.

## 6. Family comparison (how the variants differ; nothing is collapsed)

| source | operators | operands | terms | format | corruption | framing | answer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| de Varda | + - mixed | 2-3 digits | 2-3 | numeric, EN/ES/IT words, 2 story forms | all operators flipped | one-shot or none, raw | leading space, digits or words |
| Nikankin | + - * / (4 tasks) | 0..299, results <= 999 | 2 | "x+y=" no spaces | other prompt, same operator, same digit counts | bare completion | no space |
| Stolfo | + - * / and operator change | 1..300, results < 300 | 2 | 6 Q/A or equation templates | operand swap (equal digit counts) or operator change | zero-shot raw | leading space |
| MIB | + and - | 2-digit | 2 | Stolfo template | many digit-level counterfactuals | raw | no space |
| LLM_Modularity | + - | 3-digit | 2 (and 3) | symbolic and verbal | one digit of one operand | chat template + instruction | no space |

Overlaps that would inflate composition tests: Nikankin add/sub vs Stolfo add/sub vs MIB add/sub (all numeric 2-operand operand swaps; label them as one family for hold-out); de Varda numeric overlaps with LLM_Modularity add_sub_symbolic in format but not in corruption (operator flip vs digit edit). The de Varda formats are separate tasks in one cross-format family structure: the numeric task shares problems with the other five, so they are not independent, which is the point of that dataset. The Qwen digit-wise tokenisation makes most numeric answers multi-token, and the dominant uncertainty for model capacity is whether Qwen3.5-2B solves 3-digit multi-term problems and word problems often enough for the 60% both-correct threshold.

## 7. Open items

1. Zero-shot vs one-shot prefix for de Varda (config currently one-shot, as in the paper); the run-time filters decide.
2. Embedded formats: only about 52% of clean/corrupted pairs have equal length; widen the 2,000 cap if needed (pool 7,037).
3. Negative-flip exclusion changes the operator mix (rare "++", many "-" originals); alternative is to keep negatives for numeric/verbal only, which would break id matching with the story formats.
4. Nikankin and Stolfo items are our re-implementations (no released prompts), seed 42, model-independent, not the papers' exact prompts; Nikankin division is exact-quotient only.
5. format_invariant_arithmetic: licence unclear, not converted.
6. Nikankin's BibTeX is the arXiv export (OpenReview/DBLP unreachable); venue is from the repo README.
